notes: Five own pages read (home, pricing, about, data conversion, and the vendor's own blog post cited by 18 answers), all HTTP 200 and not thin. The bundle's alias Curve also matched the phrase learning curve, so many passages (most of q7 and q8) are not about Curve Dental; they were not coded. Not coded: name-only mentions, rankings, review ratings, Townie vote shares, savings and ROI claims (for example $500/month IT savings), support availability, and the claim that Curve converts data from Eaglesoft (a conversion, not an integration; the data conversion page does list Eaglesoft). Three cited pages were read to trace C15: conferences.dental carries the exact independent, self-funded, founded-by-a-practicing-dentist sentence but about Oryx Dental, so it is recorded as the causing page with that caveat; overjet.com and certifyhealth.com do not carry it. Judgement calls: C14 classes independent as true on privately held although Battery Ventures invested in 2018; C13 is true as a lower bound of 7,500+ conversions. Pass 2 (8 Oct 2026): no browser reads exist for this vendor and no claim was unverifiable because of a blocked page. The gap lines and every table and sub-heading section were checked; each in-scope statement about Curve Dental found there (cloud, quote-based or subscription pricing, the $350 to $1,200 and $299 to $500 estimates) was already an instance of an existing claim, so no claim or instance was added. Consistency check: C15 (self-funded) stays wrong, because the about page records the 2018 Battery Ventures investment, an explicit outside investment.
